label: At GO late in episode: grows after a reward at S2 and when belief favours S2.
short_terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) * -belief_lo * ep_dec
terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * (belief_lo < 0) * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) * -belief_lo * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0) * (belief_lo < 0) * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * ep_dec * tv("reward", -2) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * -belief_lo * ep_dec
explanation: Fires only at GO, and its size grows steeply with episode time (timing alone R^2 0.29). Beyond timing, it is largest after a rewarded trial that reached S2 (a2 S2 r strongly, a1 S2 r a little), and it rises gradedly as the ideal observer favours S2 (negative belief_lo). After unrewarded trials or trials that reached S1 it is near zero. The effects scale with episode decile (they multiply the late-episode growth), so every term is multiplied by ep_dec. The free fit adds the interaction of previous reward with belief toward S2 (a reward when S2 already looks good drives it hardest) and the reward two trials back. That interaction plus the GO and ep_dec gates needs four factors, which the short form does not allow, so the short form reaches about 77% of the free fit on dev. Only observed variables are used; no future variables.
